subject: Dedicated capacity stability & runbook — request for operational safeguards
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@clearshorehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearshorehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify reserved-gpu behavior and outage runbook for Dedicated

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our engineering team had two follow-ups before we can sign: clear language on queueing behavior under high contention, and an operational runbook for reserved GPUs (preemption, maintenance, and failover). We run low-latency inference for triage workflows so tail latency matters more than average throughput.

Specifically we need:
- A statement of throughput/SLOs for a 16-GPU dedicated pool under 95th and 99th percentiles.
- How Redwood prioritizes requests when burst traffic arrives: fair share vs priority lanes vs headroom.
- What automated fallbacks exist (model-variant routing, burst credits) and how they impact latency.
- A maintenance-window playbook and communications SLA (we need notice windows and graceful draining).

If you have a runbook (or template) I can share with our ops team. Procurement will also need any proposed contract language around credits/uptime remedies.

Alex
Alex Grant
Sr. Engineering Manager — Inference Platform
Clearshore Health

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@clearshorehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify reserved-gpu behavior and outage runbook for Dedicated

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list — really helpful. Attaching a first-pass runbook that addresses queueing, preemption behavior, and a proposed maintenance notification cadence (see capacity-runbook-draft.pdf). High-level answers inline below; we'll follow up with concrete SLO numbers and a short workshop with your ops team.

Inline:
- Throughput/SLOs (95/99): we publish model-variant profiles (linked in the runbook) and can commit to per-pool 95th- and 99th-percentile targets as part of a dedicated contract. Typical targets depend on model size and sequence length; recommended to scope to the production model variant to lock the SLA.

- Request prioritization: default is fair-share per-tenant within a pool, with optional priority lanes for specific routes. Priority lanes are sticky (token-based) and can guarantee lower tail latency at the cost of reduced throughput for non-priority traffic.

- Automated fallbacks: we support automatic routing to pinned model-variants (quantized or smaller architecture), and a burst credit system that allows short spikes without preemption. Burst credits are time-bounded and visible in Console analytics.

- Maintenance & draining: our standard is a 72h notice for major maintenance with a graceful drain window (configurable; default 30 minutes per instance). For customers needing stricter guarantees we can include maintenance carve-outs with additional credits.

Action items I propose:
1) Ben — can you confirm the commercial options we can include for a customer that needs 99th-percentile tail guarantees (credits, priority lane pricing, and headroom add-on)?
2) Lauren — can you pull the current sample SLA language we usually put into Dedicated contracts for reserved GPU uptime/credits?
3) Alex — would you like a 30 minute ops workshop this week to walk the runbook with your SREs?

I'll also flag this thread to our infra SRE (offline) if we need deeper kernel-level behavior notes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity-runbook-draft.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Grant <alex.grant@clearshorehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify reserved-gpu behavior and outage runbook for Dedicated

Marissa / Alex —

Quick commercial context from my side. We can offer a three-part mitigation package for customers that have strict 99th tail needs:

1) Priority lanes — priced as an add-on, reserved token slots for critical routes. Guarantees lower queuing delays by pre-allocating scheduling slices.
2) Headroom buffer — an elastically reserved buffer (10–20% of pool capacity) that can be used during bursts. Can be contracted for steady state seasons.
3) Tail credits — if we miss the agreed 99th-percentile latency target over a billing month, we apply credits (formulae differ by severity).

Notes on maintenance: for carve-outs where Clearshore requires <24h notice and strict no-preemption windows, we typically trade that for a higher monthly commit or an extended headroom buffer.

I'll draft suggested contract language and the credit formula (simple: hours_outage * monthly_commit_rate * severity_multiplier) and drop it in HubSpot under CL-8421.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/95672/CL-8421

From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@clearshorehealth.com>

Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@clearshorehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-19T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify reserved-gpu behavior and outage runbook for Dedicated

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick items before we schedule the ops workshop:

- Please send the draft contract language and the credit formula so our legal team can review.
- The runbook looks good; two asks: (a) add a short appendix with the exact Console metrics we should monitor (token queue depth, instance preemption counts, burst credit usage) and (b) include a sample incident notification template (we need the cadence and who gets paged at 5m/30m/1h).

Procurement will be running our standard SOC2 questionnaire in parallel — I attached the spreadsheet they requested (clearshore-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx).

If you can send the contract draft and the metrics appendix by Wednesday we'll aim to complete legal review the following week. After that, DocuSign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex

Attachment: clearshore-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx
